title: Curriculum Visual and Multimodal Evidence Standard
principle: Every subject and every qualification must use the visual, spatial, symbolic, audio, performance or material representations genuinely required to teach and assess its official learning outcomes. Text-only coverage is not accepted where the syllabus requires or where understanding depends on a non-text representation. Visuals must teach, be interpreted, be constructed or be used as evidence; decoration does not count.
requirements: Map each official learning outcome to required representation modes before lesson authoring.

Include the exact diagram, graph, sketch, map, chart, timeline, annotated image, specimen, model, notation, score, composition, source extract, practical layout or other artefact needed by that outcome.
Teach learners how to read, interpret, label, construct, annotate, compare and evaluate each required representation where the syllabus expects those skills.
Provide worked examples and independent practice using the representation, with accessible text alternatives and answer rationales.
Keep assets versioned, source-attributed where externally sourced, legible on mobile and desktop, printable where useful, and bundled for offline use when the lesson is marked offline-ready.
Do not fabricate data, historical artefacts, artworks, maps, quotations, scientific images or exam sources. Clearly label original teaching diagrams and illustrative data.
Do not force irrelevant visuals into an outcome. Select the modality that carries the subject knowledge accurately.

sciences: graphs with units, scales and uncertainty
economics: tables and flow models; all axes, shifts and labels taught explicitly
music: listening maps and waveform/spectrogram views when relevant

accessibility: Every non-decorative visual has meaningful alt text or an equivalent structured description.
Colour is never the only carrier of meaning.
Labels, line styles, symbols and units remain distinguishable in grayscale and low-data modes.
Provide a text or tabular equivalent for essential information.
offline: Bundle or cache required lesson visuals with their lesson pack.
No essential diagram may depend on a third-party URL at runtime.
Record asset checksum, source, licence/permission and version for external assets.
Offline-ready status is blocked if any required asset is missing.

rejectIf: required visual is only mentioned in prose but not supplied
graph lacks axis labels/units/scale or declared illustrative data
image/source lacks provenance or rights status
art/music/performance subject has been reduced to generic prose when the official outcome requires making or analysing artefacts
asset is decorative and not connected to an outcome
lesson claims offline readiness while a required asset is remote or missing
